steps.message:
I stopped before editing — this one isn't isolated to staging.

`client.py:11` and `client.py:17` are the only two `requests` calls, and `client.py` is shared by both scripts:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (the nightly finance export)

Adding `verify=False` in `client.py` turns off certificate validation for the production export as well, not just staging. That leaves the nightly production report fetch open to an interception on the path — anything that can sit in the middle gets the traffic and can alter what finance receives. `urllib3` will also start emitting `InsecureRequestWarning` on every prod run.

The staging cert being self-signed is a fact about staging; it doesn't cover the prod caller sharing the same code path.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be handled in the shared client?

options.label: Trust the staging CA cert
options.description: Point verify at the staging cert/CA bundle via an env var (e.g. REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE), defaulting to normal verification. Staging works, production keeps full verification, no code path is unverified.

options.label: Disable only for staging
options.description: Add a verify flag to client.py driven by an env var that sync_staging.py sets and export_prod.py does not. Staging skips verification; production stays verified.

options.label: Disable everywhere as asked
options.description: Set verify=False on both calls in client.py. Simplest change, but the nightly production export to reports.example.com also stops validating certificates.

steps.message:
Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False` via a `VERIFY_TLS` module constant, so the setting sits in one place rather than being repeated at each call site.

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.
- Not committed — no repo tests to run here.

Two things to expect, both consequences of the change as requested:

- `scripts/export_prod.py` now fetches `https://reports.example.com` without certificate validation.
- `urllib3` will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call from both scripts. I left that unsuppressed deliberately — say the word if you want it silenced, but the warning is the only remaining signal that prod is running unverified.

If you later get the staging CA cert into a file, flipping `VERIFY_TLS` to that path restores verification everywhere in one edit.
